body.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\), determine the smallest deterministic penalty sequence \(\ell_n\ge1\) for which a fully data-driven estimator and confidence interval, not given \(\kappa\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), or \(r_{en}\), attain uniform risk and honest expected length at most \(C\ell_n\rho_n\) over compact ranges of these indices; prove a matching adaptation lower bound for \(\ell_n\).
body.justification: The oracle theorem exposes but does not resolve the cost of learning which of the four obstructions is active.
body.gap: The frozen model supplies no observable certificate for all unknown global approximation radii.
body.consumer: Its resolution would determine whether validation-driven clipping and honest intervals require a logarithmic adaptation penalty.

obligation.what_is_open: The smallest adaptation penalty and its matching lower bound when the tail exponent, both shell constants, and all three nuisance radii are unknown.
obligation.obstruction: The oracle threshold uses unknown quantities in three competing scales. The frozen adaptation handle supplies no observable uniform upper certificate for the global approximation errors, and those certificates cannot be recovered from validation data without further structure on the public predictors. Honest interval adaptation additionally needs a between-class testing argument absent from the fixed-index lower families.
obligation.attempted: A dyadic Lepski comparison controls stochastic differences between clipped scores, but its deterministic biases contain \(r_{1n}\lambda^{\kappa/2}\), \(r_{1n}r_{en}/\lambda\), and \(r_{0n}r_{en}\), none of which has a uniformly estimable upper certificate in the frozen model. Empirical shell counts require control of the unknown propensity approximation error, which is itself an unidentified radius entering the threshold choice.
obligation.partial_result:
With \(\kappa\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), and the certified radii supplied,
\texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper}, \texttt{lem:median-risk-upgrade}, and
\texttt{thm:honest-interval-frontier} attain risk and expected length of order
\(\rho_n\), so the oracle adaptation penalty is \(1\). No claim about the
unknown-index penalty follows from the frozen primitives.
